questions.explain: Request level (llm_audit_log — billing, cost, latency), action level (agent_actions — debugging, compliance, eval), prompt level (prompt_audit — forensics, 90-day retention, restricted access) — separate tables and retentions, never mixed.
options: One table for everything
Only the request level matters
Request, action, and prompt levels in separate tables with different retentions
Audit logs are optional for AI apps
questions.q: What are the three audit granularities and why are they separate?

questions.explain: Narrow request rows go in the request transaction; bulky prompt payloads are written by a background queue worker; write-path indexing stays minimal; delayed durability applies to the prompt tier only.
options: Narrow rows in the request transaction, prompt payloads via background worker, minimal write indexing, delayed durability for prompt tier only
Write everything synchronously in the chat path
Skip audit writes under load
Use delayed durability for billing-critical rows
questions.q: How are audit writes kept off the critical path?

questions.explain: Each row's chain_hash commits to all previous rows, so altering history breaks every later link; a nightly job verifies the chain, daily terminal hashes are anchored externally, and SQL Server Audit covers privileged access.
options: Trust the application
Encrypt the audit table
Delete old rows frequently
Hash-chained rows with nightly verification plus external anchoring of daily terminal hashes, paired with SQL Server Audit
questions.q: How is the audit log made tamper-evident?

questions.explain: Pre-build incident timelines (everything one user did in a window), blast-radius analysis (tenants affected by a bad prompt version), and cost-spike forensics — during an incident is the wrong time to write forensic SQL.
options: Write forensic queries during the incident
Pre-built procedures: incident timelines, blast-radius analysis, cost-spike forensics
Forensics are impossible with audit logs
Only check the most recent row
questions.q: Which forensic queries should be pre-built?

questions.explain: Audit logs concentrate sensitive data, so access itself needs oversight: quarterly reviews of who holds the support-lead role, automated evidence gathering, and aggressive revocation — the hardest permission to keep.
options: Grant audit access to everyone
Annual reviews are enough
Quarterly access reviews with automated evidence and aggressive revocation
Audit access needs no oversight
questions.q: Why do audit logs need quarterly access reviews?

title: Audit Logging Every AI Action in SQL Server
